author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Philippine forensic teams began identifying victims recovered from the burned MV June Aster on Saturday as authorities reported at least 35 deaths and more than 50 people still missing. Bodies were brought to temporary processing tents at the port in Coron, where relatives waited for information about passengers who had not been accounted for.

The ferry was carrying more than 130 people when it caught fire near the end of a journey lasting more than 20 hours. Firefighters entered the vessel Friday after extinguishing the blaze, gaining access to sections that had been unreachable because of intense heat and thick smoke. The Coast Guard said burned remains were found in the economy accommodation area.

Investigators are also working to determine the cause. The Maritime Industry Authority said survivor accounts included reports of two explosions shortly before the fire, but officials have not established what produced them. Identification and the search for missing passengers remain the immediate priorities. The casualty figures may change as teams examine the vessel and reconcile passenger information.
dek: Forensic teams are processing remains recovered from the MV June Aster after the death toll reached at least 35 and more than 50 people remained missing.
headline: Philippines begins identifying ferry-fire victims as dozens remain missing
